# Layergram 2.0.6 — Keyboard resume and installation reliability

Layergram's Android and iOS system keyboards let you compose and preview
encrypted messages inside the messaging apps you already use. Private text
stays in the keyboard; the other app receives the encrypted text carrier only
after explicit insertion.

This release fixes iOS biometric keyboard reopening, keeps navigation labels
readable in unfolded layouts, and separates a fresh iOS installation from an
in-place update: updates retain the identity, while a complete uninstall
requires deliberate identity creation or restoration.

The system keyboard remains an opt-in experimental feature on both mobile
platforms. Ordinary builds keep its compile-time flags off. The source build
and consent steps are documented in [the keyboard guide](https://github.com/layergram/layergram/blob/v2.0.6%2B33/SYSTEM_KEYBOARD.md).

The [source build instructions](https://github.com/layergram/layergram/blob/v2.0.6%2B33/README.md#getting-started)
include the pinned toolchains and native protocol-backend preparation. Local
Android builds use a debug certificate when no signing configuration is
provided; official APKs use Layergram's dedicated direct-download certificate.
Verify official downloads against the accompanying SHA-256 inventory.

Protocol v3 and its existing forward-secrecy modes are unchanged. Automated
checks and device validation are not a substitute for an independent security
audit; the [threat model](https://github.com/layergram/layergram/blob/v2.0.6%2B33/THREAT_MODEL.md)
describes the security assumptions and limits.
